title: Print 1 to N using the loop variable
idea: The classic use: print each number from 1 up to N. Put range(1, N+1) together with print(i). Build and trace it.

exercises.explanation: range(1, 6) is 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 (stop 6 excludes itself). Printing i shows each number.
range(1, 4) counts 1, 2, 3. Each pass prints the current i.
To include 10, stop is 11 (one past). range(1, 11) prints 1 through 10.
Header range(1, 4) first, then the indented print(i). That prints 1, 2, 3.

exercises.prompt:
What shows?

n = 3
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    print(i)
exercises.explanation: n is 3, so range(1, n + 1) is range(1, 4): 1, 2, 3. Using n + 1 as stop makes it count 1 through n.

exercises.prompt: range(1, n + 1) counts from 1 up to and including n.
exercises.explanation: Because stop is excluded, you add 1 to n so n itself is included. A very common pattern for '1 to n'.

exercises.prompt: You wrote range(1, n) to print 1 to n but it stops one short. The fix?
options: Use range(1, n + 1) so n is included
exercises.explanation: Stop is excluded, so range(1, n) misses n. Add 1: range(1, n + 1). Classic off-by-one fix.
The f-string drops in i each pass: Round 1 through Round 5. The loop variable makes each line different.

exercises.prompt: Putting i inside an f-string lets each pass show its own number.
exercises.explanation: Yes — f"Round {i}" uses the current i, so lines read Round 1, Round 2, and so on. f-strings plus the loop variable are a great pair.

exercises.prompt: A countdown screen needs labels Step 1 to Step 4. Which loop?
exercises.explanation: range(1, 5) gives 1, 2, 3, 4, and the f-string labels each: Step 1 through Step 4.
